difficulty_notes: Requires updating after strong privacy safeguards while retaining concern about trust, uptake, and residual re-identification risk.
Requires distinguishing suppression of dissent from narrow action against harmful false factual claims with procedural controls.
Requires recognising that structural inequality remains relevant without ignoring concrete evidence that the proposed system reduced several original risks.
Requires updating despite the emotionally salient fact that monitoring occurs in private rooms.
Requires not treating child-data sensitivity as a trump card that blocks all updating after relevant safeguards.
Requires updating in a domain where residual moral concern is very strong and easy to over-weight.
Requires updating in a high-stakes housing context without treating residual fairness concern as unchanged.
Requires updating despite the salient concern that reading analytics can chill intellectual freedom.
Requires updating while retaining concern about student labelling and educational self-concept.
Requires updating despite residual concern that central data-access review can become unfair gatekeeping.
Requires updating despite the salient bodily-autonomy concern created by mandatory wearable sensors.
Requires updating despite residual concern about automated influence over conditions inside private homes.
